title: VoipProvider contract for reselling, a mock provider and a local call simulator
goal: Define everything the platform needs from a phone provider in one interface, and make every call flow testable on this machine without a real provider.
why: services/voip-provider.ts VoipProvider has call, number and markup methods but nothing for sub-accounts, usage records or call-bridge (ADR-001 section 6 items 2, 3, 6); Plivo outbound points at a route that does not exist; no test can exercise inbound or outbound flows end to end (CALL-AUTOMATION 4.4 item 8).
steps: Extend VoipProvider (READINESS-PLAN 4.13): createSubAccount({ tenantId, name }) -> { subAccountId, authId, authTokenEnc }, closeSubAccount, placeCall({ mode: softphone|bridge, from, to, agentNumber?, agentIdentity?, callbackBaseUrl, record }) (replaces initiateCall; keep initiateCall as a wrapper), fetchUsage({ subAccountId, since }) -> normalized records { providerCallId, direction, to, from, startedAt, durationSeconds, billedSeconds, cost, currency }, clientIdentity(userId) (one naming rule used for tokens and ring markup: `u_${userId without hyphens}`), plus existing methods. Twilio and Plivo implementations: implement what is straightforward with fetch (sub-accounts: Twilio Accounts API, Plivo Subaccount API; usage: Twilio Calls list filtered by account, Plivo CDR) and throw NotImplementedForProvider for the rest; fix Plivo answer_url to point at an existing route (/voip/xml/outbound to be added in R302, so make it configurable).
mock-provider.ts: in-memory/KV-backed provider that records calls and returns deterministic ids; selected when VOIP_PROVIDER=mock or TEST_MODE and no credentials.

simulator.ts + routes/test.ts (TEST_MODE only): POST /test/voip/simulate { scenario: inbound_answered|inbound_missed|inbound_voicemail|outbound_answered|outbound_no_answer, to, from, durationSeconds } that posts the same signed form callbacks the real provider would send (signed with the mock secret) to the callback routes in order, so backend and e2e tests drive full flows.
tests: backend/test/voip-provider-contract.test.ts: the same contract suite runs against MockProvider and, with mocked fetch, Twilio and Plivo: placeCall bridge and softphone request shapes, createSubAccount request shape, fetchUsage normalisation from recorded JSON fixtures, clientIdentity rule shared by token and markup.
acceptance: Simulator drives a missed-call scenario that creates the call-back task (existing recipe).
gate: cd backend && npx vitest run   # pass: 0 failed files and passed >= the last merged count (1296 on 2026-10-14)
goLiveVerify: Real sub-account creation and usage API behaviour for the G1 provider.
notes: Before editing read: this batch file, docs/readiness/READINESS-PLAN.md sections 0 and the design note for this area, desktop/audit/fix/FIX-PLAN.md sections 3-4 (executor rules, worktree bootstrap with node_modules junctions; never npm install inside a worktree unless the batch adds a dependency, and then only in the main checkout by the orchestrator).

Backend tests follow the existing pattern (see backend/test/voip-callbacks.test.ts): import env, createExecutionContext, waitOnExecutionContext, applyD1Migrations from cloudflare:test; applyD1Migrations(env.MASTER_DB, env.TEST_MIGRATIONS) in beforeAll; POST /api/v1/test/reset; call worker.fetch(request, env, ctx). isolatedStorage is false and singleWorker true, so use unique ids/emails per test file.

Read docs/decisions/ADR-001-voip.md (sections 4, 6, 7) and docs/CALL-AUTOMATION.md (sections 2, 3, 4) before editing; they are the specification. G1 (provider choice and India shape) is not signed: everything here stays behind the VoipProvider interface.
